huaer.basis: Repertoire is large (over a hundred ling tunes in the Hehuang area, over a hundred annual festivals, national inheritors such as 朱仲禄, 马金山, 马俊), and regional cassettes and discs circulate in the northwest, but almost none of it is catalogued: one internationally issued field album (Naxos World 2019, 46 tracks across five peoples, only some of them hua'er) and scattered tracks by trained singers (苏平, 朱仲禄, 龚琳娜) on mainland releases. Range is a rough guess at issued, findable hua'er tracks, not a catalogue count.

kulintang.basis: No source counts recordings. Discogs lists 99 release hits for 'kulintang', most of them jazz or experimental records using the instrument; the ensemble releases found are about a dozen archive and community albums (Folkways 1961, UP Department of Music Research 1977 and 1988, Lyrichord Maranao volumes c. 1979, World Kulintang Institute 1994, Smithsonian Folkways 2021), each of 10–30 short tracks, plus unreleased archive holdings (Maceda collection) and local Philippine and Sabah recordings. The repertoire itself is small: a handful of Maguindanao rhythmic modes and a dozen-odd Maranao named pieces, so an insider's essential list is about 15 pieces/performances.

malhun.basis: No catalogue counts malhun recordings. The Moroccan Ministry of Culture issued a 3-CD malhun set (mentioned in an M&A review of the 2001-2002 Anthologie de la Musique Marocaine); the genre's text corpus runs to many hundreds of qasidas by named poets from the 16th to 20th centuries (French Wikipedia lists dozens of poets and printed anthologies, e.g. Guessous 2008/2014). Recordings exist mainly as radio archives and cassettes by singers such as Houcine Toulali (1924-1998), so the issued-track range is a judgement. Core: a few dozen qasidas that every malhun audience knows (e.g. Chamaa, Herraz Aouicha), each recorded by several singers.

garbaanddandiyaraa.basis: Garba is a large commercial regional market: every Navratri brings new non-stop volumes (Ramzat from 2017, Rangtaali 2017 and 2019 with 36 tracks on volume 2, many more from Gujarati labels such as Sur Sagar and Red Ribbon), plus re-recordings of the same traditional songs by star singers (Atul Purohit, Falguni Pathak, Praful Dave, Hemant Chauhan, Kirtidan Gadhvi), and 1970s LPs (Polydor 1976, HMV 1978). No catalogue total was found; the range is a rough count of issued tracks including the many duplicate versions. The core is the few dozen traditional songs every Navratri set returns to.

mahagita.basis: The repertoire itself is bounded: an 1870 anthology lists 1,062 song titles in 27 genres and the 1954–61 state edition standardises 169 songs. Issued recordings are a few international releases (Smithsonian Folkways 2003, the UNESCO/Auvidis harp CD, Muriel Williamson collection volumes, Inle Myint Maung's multi-volume 'Mahagita By Burmese Harp' series) plus an uncounted Burmese domestic cassette/CD and radio output by classical singers and saung, piano and pattala players; the range is a judgement, not a catalogue count. Core: roughly the most-performed kyo, bwe, thachingan, patpyo and yodaya songs a Burmese musician would expect to know.

kobzardumy.basis: Repertoire is small: dumy are a closed set of Cossack-era subjects (the Encyclopedia of Ukraine names six as examples; the 1908–1910 cylinders hold about a dozen subjects). Archive side: the Kolessa/Slastion/Kvitka cylinder collection on Commons has 24 duma rows, plus later Soviet-era field and radio recordings of the few surviving traditional kobzari not counted here. Revival side: a few dozen kobzar-revival performers (Kytasty, Kushpet, Fedynsky, Kompanichenko, Drach, the kobzar guilds), each recording a handful of dumy. The range is a judgement, not a catalogue total; core = the dozen classic subjects in one or two good recordings each.

tarantella.basis: Archive side: Lomax and Carpitella's 1954-55 field tapes (Rounder Italian Treasury: Salento, Calabria, Naples/Campania volumes; Folkways FE 4265 holds five tarantella items of 20 tracks), Folkways' Italian-American volumes (Calabria Bella 1979, Festa Italiana) and 78s by Italian-American dance orchestras. Revival side: Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino alone has about 18 albums since 1975, plus Officina Zoè, NCCP, Eugenio Bennato/Taranta Power, Alla Bua, Uccio Aloisi, Tammurriata di Scafati and the yearly Notte della Taranta concerts since 1998, each album carrying several pizziche or tarantellas. Range is a reasoned guess, not a catalogue count; core is what a Salento or Campania player would call essential across the regional forms.

iraqimaqam.basis: The repertoire is about 56 named maqam compositions (Rough Trade on Hamid Al-Saadi), each recorded many times since 78 rpm days by a few dozen named singers (Wikipedia lists 27), with Muhammad al-Qubanchi the most recorded artist of the early record era (Qatar Digital Library). Commercial albums outside Iraq are few ('one of a handful of commercially released albums in the genre', Rough Trade), but Iraqi radio and television archives and 78s add many more. A judgement, not a count: roughly 800–4000 recorded maqam performances, of which about 50 (the main maqams by Qubanchi, Yusuf Omar, Nazem al-Ghazali, al-A‘dhami, Farida, Hamid al-Saadi) would be called essential.
